title: Area, perimeter and volume quiz
description: Twelve questions drawn at random from a bank of sixteen, covering circles, Pythagoras, surface area, volume and units. Use $\pi = 3.14$ unless told otherwise.

questions.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle with radius $7\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.
Find the area of a circle with **diameter** $12\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.
questions.explanation: Halve the diameter first: $r = 6$. Then $A = 3.14 \times 36 = 113.04\ \text{cm}^2$. Using 12 as the radius would give four times too much.
The diameter runs right across the circle through the centre, and is twice the radius.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides $5\ \text{cm}$ and $12\ \text{cm}$. Find the hypotenuse.
A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse $10\ \text{cm}$ and one shorter side $6\ \text{cm}$. Find the other shorter side.
questions.explanation: $10^2 - 6^2 = 100 - 36 = 64$, so the side is $\sqrt{64} = 8\ \text{cm}$. The hypotenuse is given, so you subtract.
The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and always the longest.

questions.prompt: **A triangle with sides $6\ \text{cm}$, $7\ \text{cm}$ and $10\ \text{cm}$ is right-angled.**
questions.explanation: $6^2 + 7^2 = 36 + 49 = 85$, but $10^2 = 100$. They are not equal, so the triangle is not right-angled.

questions.prompt: Find the total surface area of a cuboid $4\ \text{cm} \times 5\ \text{cm} \times 6\ \text{cm}$.
**Click the curved surface** of this cylinder.
questions.explanation: Unrolled, the curved surface is a rectangle $2\pi r$ wide by $h$ tall, so its area is $2\pi r h$.

questions.prompt: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius $5\ \text{cm}$ and height $8\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.
Set the sliders to build a cuboid measuring $4 \times 3 \times 2\ \text{cm}$, then read off its volume.
A tank measures $30\ \text{cm} \times 20\ \text{cm} \times 25\ \text{cm}$. How many litres does it hold?

questions.explanation: $6 \times 1000 = 6000\ \text{MB}$ — a megabyte is smaller, so the number grows.
$1$ litre $= 1000\ \text{cm}^3$ and $1\ \text{m}^3 = 100^3 = 1\,000\,000\ \text{cm}^3$ — all three dimensions scale by 100.

questions.prompt: Match each shape to the right formula.

left.text: Curved surface area of a cylinder

questions.explanation: Volume is the circle's area times the height; the curved surface is the circumference times the height. Keeping that distinction clear is most of this topic.

questions.prompt: A compound-shape problem, one step at a time.
questions.scenario: A shape is a rectangle $10\ \text{cm}$ by $6\ \text{cm}$ with a semicircle of diameter $6\ \text{cm}$ joined to one short end. Use $\pi = 3.14$.

steps.prompt: What is the area of the rectangle, in $\text{cm}^2$?
The semicircle has diameter $6\ \text{cm}$. What is its radius, in cm?
What is the area of the semicircle, in $\text{cm}^2$? (Half of $\pi r^2$.)
What is the total area of the shape, in $\text{cm}^2$?

questions.explanation: Split a compound shape into pieces you recognise, work out each one, then combine. Total area $= 60 + 14.13 = 74.13\ \text{cm}^2$.
